To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Dam methylation-dependent repression of the std fimbriae operon is required for efficient Salmonella invasion of intestinal epithelial cell and that crosstalk between the virulence loci std and SPI- 1 plays a role in intestinal infection.

1) the std operon, which encodes fimbrial proteins and is expressed in the ileum, is a target of Dam methylation-dependent regulation; and 2) the std operons and SPI-1 are under Dam methylation-dependent crosstalk, with the former repressing the latter in the caecal compartment of the gut.

the std fimbriation operon is a new locus involved in regulation of Salmonella invasion and that this regulation is mediated by a crosstalk between the std and SPI-2 loci, which is dependent on Dam methylation and the ileum-specific expression of std.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the Dam methylase in the regulation of virulence genes in Salmonella.
the role of the Dam methylation system in the regulation of virulence gene expression in Salmonella enterica.
the role of Dam methylation in regulation of Salmonella pathogenic island 1 (spi-1) and its interrelationship with the std fimbriae.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Dam methylation regulates SPI-1 through its effect on expression of the std fimbriae operon, and that StdE and StdE products are required to repress SPI-1 in a Dam− genetic background.
std operon is involved in regulation of SPI-1, and that this regulation is dependent on the Dam methylation system.
the Dam methylation system is involved in the control of the SPI- 1 operon, through the regulation of the std fimbria operon.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
std and SPI- 1 are under Dam-dependent regulation and that this control is essential for virulence.
Dam-dependent regulation of std and SPI- 1 in the Salmonella genome is part of a regulatory network which ensures the expression of the SPI- 1 invasion machinery only in the ileum.

Dam-dependent control of std expression in the ileum is required to permit SPI-1 expression and invasion, while Dam-dependent repression of StdE/StdF in the caecium is required to permit expression of SPI-2, which is required for Salmonella survival in this compartment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Dam methylation-dependent repression of the std operon in the ileum is required for efficient invasion of epithelial intestinal cells.
the std operon, a locus that is involved in intestinal colonization, also plays an important role in the pathogenesis of Salmonella.
crosstalk between virulence loci is a common mechanism to coordinate expression of virulence genes in the course of infection.
